value.rationale: Two-run subsequence ideals are canonical examples of upward-closed regular languages; asking for both opposite temporal orders is a natural simultaneous-pattern constraint. The exact two-parameter formula quantifies a strict loss against the naive product DFA, including an explicit balanced family with size \(3t(t+1)\), and the four-region quotient structure explains which prefix-progress combinations can coexist. This is a motivated complete infinite-family state-complexity classification, not an arbitrary table or routine restatement of a worst-case bound.
